mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which leads to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as discounting of expected cash flows tightens.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS rise < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs over the next quarter is associated with stronger consumer demand, which drives a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the next 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS growth ≥50,000 (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of 2% or more over the next month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing signals contractionary expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥2% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the predicted HOUST decline (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production index) falls below 110 over the next 2 months, supply-side pressures lead to a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is positive when INDPRO < 110 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% in the following month, accompanied by a simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS, creates conflicting expectations that drive a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND FEDFUNDS increases in the next month
regime_hint: Unemployment rate surprise low with rising rates
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive when both conditions occur (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 for two consecutive months, it signals labor market strength that supports a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via consumer spending amplification.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the PAYEMS expansion period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in GDPC1 (GDP) of at least 2% followed by a rebound in the next week creates a contrarian opportunity, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates stabilization.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by ≥2% in a month then rises in the following week
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite the pattern (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL (CPI) inflation above 2.5%, a 20-day S&P 500 forward return is negative as investors discount future cash flows more aggressively, expecting higher real rates.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (p < 0.05).
